title: HelperSSHProbeParams
description: One credential test against one host, asked of the helper that dials. It carries the SAME destination every other op takes — resolved address, account, credential reference and route — rather than its own copy of the address, so a probe of a host behind a jump host is a probe of the host a person named. A probe that carried loose fields would be the one place a route could be forgotten, and a direct dial to an address that is only reachable through a bastion fails as 'unreachable' — a network problem, where the truth is a hop.

destination.description: Where to dial, what to authenticate with, and which hosts it is reached through. Resolved by the coordinator, which reads ~/.ssh/config and holds the credential binding (plan §3).

acceptOnTrust.description: The coordinator's answer to 'may a host key this host has never presented be recorded'. It is the CALLER's decision travelling with the request: the coordinator sets it only after the accept flow it already owns has run (connections.trustHostKey), and the helper then asks for the write through trust-host-key. A helper therefore cannot turn 'ask the user' into 'trust it', and a `changed` verdict never reaches that write whatever this says — a changed key is the one signature of a machine in the middle.
